2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:

sentences.text: The Respondent No.2 the owner and the petitioner were both sitting in the seats behind the driver while an employee of the Respondent No.2 was siting in the front seat, by the side of the driver.

The car met with an accident when the petitioner was in brief phase of sleep,
which gave him no chance to escape the accident or witness it in person.
Due to the accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and unconscious.

The petitioner learnt in retrospect that the said car in which he was traveling back from Chennai, the driver of the Car driven the same rashly and negligently and dashed against the Truck vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-C-4687 which was stated to have been parked on the National Highway, wrongly.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital,
Vaniambadi and thereafter shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengauru and then shifted to Sagar Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
He has spent more than Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical treatment, conveyance and the nourishment expenses.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as an Architect and was earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

3. The Respondent No.1 is the driver, the Respondent No.2 is the owner and Respondent No.3 is the Insurer of the Honda City car and Respondent No.4 is the driver, Respondent No.5 is the owner and Respondent No.6 is the Insurer of the truck.
Therefore, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
4. Despite of service of notice Respondent No.1 and 5 remained absent, hence they are placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 to 4 and 6 appeared before the court through their respective counsels.
But, only respondent No.2, 3 and 6 filed objections to the main petition.
In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2/owner of Honda City Car, it denied the averements made in the petition.
It admitted that the Honda City Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-Z- 9024 belongs to Respondent No.2.
The said vehicle was covered with insurance policy insured by Respondent No.3.
It admitted the accident and registration of case.

Hence, among these and other grounds,
Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.3/insurer of Honda City car, it denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car.
Further it has denied the involvement of the car and manner of accident.
Further it admits the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Car in question infavor of respondent No.2.

Further it contended that the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured respondent No.2 in the present case as the petitioner Raghavendra Ramarao Kulhalli vs Umesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152634601/
3 was travelling in the private car for hire and reward in violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.

my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 8. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that on 11.06.2009 at about 4.00 p.m. while he was travelling as inmate in the car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-Z-9024 near Vaniambadi town, driven rash and negligent manner by its driver and dashed against the Truck bearing Reg. No.KA-01-C- 4687 which had been parked on the National Highway, wrongly, leading to his injuries.
9. The Respondent No.1 being driver of car, respondent No.4 being driver and respondent No.5 being RC owner of the Lorry did not contest the matter.

The owner and insurer of the Car i.e.,
Respondent No.2 and 3 and the insurer of the Lorry i.e., Respondent No.6 have contested the matter.

10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and he has filed his chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the petition averments and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.
P.W.1 has re-

Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-3 are the certified copies of Complaint, FIR and Charge sheet in Tamil Language, Ex

Ex.P.6 is the Certified copy of Form- AIR (2 in nos.), ExP.7 is the medical bills, Ex.P.8 is the Prescriptions, Ex.P.9 is the X-rays, Ex.P.10 is the MRI scan films, Ex.P.11 is the Income Tax returns copies for the year 2007-2008 to 2019-2020, Ex.P.12 is the Reconstitution of Partnership deed dated 08.05.2006, Ex.P.13 is the copies of Income tax returns of the firm for the year 2007-2008 to Raghavendra Ramarao Kulhalli vs Umesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152634601/

11.

It is well settled principle of law that in a claim for compensation under sec. 166 of MV Act, the claimant has to prove the accident only on preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2011 SAR (Civil)
319 between Kusum & Ors vs Satbir & Ors.
12. Keeping the aforesaid principles in mind considered the evidence on record.

Upon careful perusal of Ex.P.1(a) and Ex.P.2(a) English translated copies of Ex.P.1 and 2 Complaint and FIR in Tamil language, they show that the case was registered against the driver of the Honda City Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-Z-9024.

Ex.P-3 is the certified copy of the Charge sheet in Tamil language and Ex.P.3(a) its English translated copy which shows that the Vaniyambadi Taluk Police have submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending Car for the offences bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-Z-9024 punishable under Sec.279, 338, 304(A) of IPC.

Ex.P.4 is the Accident Register,
wherein the history has been mentioned as 'Alleged H/ o RTA at 4.10 p.m on 11.06.2009 near Vaniambadi Murugar Temple-Tenderness in lumbar inability to move both lower limb-A lacerated wound on left upper eye lid- Tenderness in chest'.
Ex.P.5 is the further statement of PW.1 which shows that he had narrated the manner of accident before the IO.
13. The Ex.P.6 Form-AIR of Honda City Car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-Z-9024.

The said report shows that the car's front W/S glass completely broken, front body completely damaged, Engine Bannet,
A/C condenser damaged, Radiator water pump damaged, H/L, indicator light broken, front top roof damaged, dash board damaged, Front body sheel bend and twisted, both side doors damaged.

14. Further, petitioner examined Dr. Pratap Kumar Pani as P.W.2 and he also re

In the cross- examination, P.W.1 specifically says that as on the date of accident, himself, the driver and Shenoy were in the car.

PW.1 has admitted that he was travelling in the company car.

He further admitted that the said road was national highway.
He further says that since he had gone into to state of sleep he did not know the manner of accident.
He learnt that the accident had happened because of the lorry driver carelessness as he had parked the lorry on the road.

18. The Respondent No.1 has examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.R.2 and Ex.R.3.
The respondent No.6 has examined one witness as RW.2 and got marked five documents at Ex.R.4 to 8.
The respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW.3 and got marked seven documents at Ex.R.9 to Ex.R.15.
The evidence of the RW.1 to 3 would not be deciding factor for negligence as they were not eye witnesses to the accident.
But, they are the official witnesses.

19. The petitioner has filed the claim petition against the respondents alleging that while he was proceeding in a car bearing No.KA-04-Z-9024, the driver of the said car drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the truck bearing No.KA-01-C-4687 which was wrongly parked on National Highway.
As such drivers of both the vehicles have contributed for the accident.
As per FIR and charge sheet, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car, the accident has occurred.

20. In the case of Mohandas Nair (Supra) the Hon'ble Apex Court held that mere parking of vehicle on public road without taking precaution is clear negligence on the part of the driver of parked vehicle.
21. In the case on hand, it is not in dispute that the driver of the truck bearing No.KA-01-C-4687 had parked his lorry on the public road i.e., National Highway.
The respondents have not chosen to lead evidence of drivers of both the vehicles i.e., car and truck.
They are the best persons to speak about the manner of accident and negligence aspect is concerned.
But they have not stepped into witness box to prove their non negligence.
The allegation against the driver of the truck is without indicator or parking lights parked the lorry on the public road.
If he had taken sufficient caution and parked the vehicle with necessary indication, he would have denied the allegation made against him.

But,
though he has appeared through his counsel, he has not chosen to file written statement and not chosen to stepped into witness box.
As such he has admitted his negligence.
The police documents available on record do not show that the lorry was parked by taking precaution.

The respondent No.4 driver of the truck and respondent No.5 the owner of the truck have not placed any materials to show that the lorry had been parked with tail lights or blinkers or self radiating triangles or guard or other devise to warn the vehicles.

By considering all these facts, it is crystal clear that lorry had been parked on the public road without taking any precaution and the driver of the car had dashed against the said lorry from back side.
Therefore, the driver of the truck had contributed for the accident.
22. Further as discussed above upon going through the entire materials available on record, it shows that the Charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the Car.

As per the contents of the police Raghavendra Ramarao Kulhalli vs Umesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152634601/
7 documents the driver of the car drove his car with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the parked lorry from its behind.
The driver of the car had not challenged the charge sheet.
It shows that he admitted the contents of the charge sheet.

These aspects show that there is gross negligence on part the driver of the car and for the aforesaid reasons there is gross negligence on part of the driver of the lorry who parked on the road without precaution.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the driver (Respondent No.1) of the car attributed 50% of negligence towards the said accident.
Further, the driver (Respondent No.4) of the Truck attributed 50% of the negligence towards the said accident.

23. Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the car and negligence act of the driver of the lorry and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'In the Affirmative'.
24. Issue No.2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver and negligent act of the driver of the truck the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
25. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 53 years.
He has not produced any document to prove his age.
But, as per the accident register i.e. Ex.P.4 the age of the Petitioner is shown as 55 years.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 55 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
26. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as Architect and was earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.11 IT returns acknowledgment from the year 2007-2008 to 2019-2020.
The accident took place in the year 2009.
As per the IT returns form for the year 2009-2010, his gross income per anuum is Rs.2,84,583/- and his income tax was deducted Rs.14,720 /- p.a.
After deducting the tax his income would be Rs.2,69,863/-.
If the said amount divides for 12 months it would be Rs.22,488/-.
Therefore, Rs.22,488/- p.m. is taken for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
27. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
 I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
28.

The Accident register i.e., Ex.P-4 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Tenderness in lumbar inability to move both lower limb- Raghavendra Ramarao Kulhalli vs Umesh on 8 April, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152634601/
8
2. A lacerated wound on left upper eye lid 3. Tenderness in chest.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
29.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
30.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 12.06.2009 to 23.06.2009.
Further, P.W.2 Dr.Pratap Kumar Pani has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
The Ex.P.14 discharge summary also justify the same.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 12 days.
31. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.45,000/- under this head (@ Rs.22,488/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
32.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
33. The Petitioner has deposed that he spent more than Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 45 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.7 which is totally amounting to Rs.6,63,625/-.
I have gone through the medical bills.
The Sl.No.1 and 2 at Ex.P.7 are advance receipts for amount of Rs.1,00,000/- and Rs.7,000/- respectively.
PW.1 also admitted in his cross-examination that these bills are advance bills.
Therefore those receipts are to be deducted from the total amount.
This bill No.3, 5, 7 and 13 are pertaining to one Girish.
In the cross examination of PW.1, he admitted the same.

Hence those receipts are to be deducted from the Raghavendra Ramarao Kulhalli vs Umesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152634601/
9 total amount.
PW.1 further admitted that bill No.23 interim bill amount is included in Bill No.27.
Therefore said bill No.23 is to be deducted from the total amount.
Hence the amount of Rs.2,38,775/- mentioned in Sl.No.23 shall not be considered.
As such the medical bills at Sl.No.1, 2 3, 5, 7, 13 and 23 are not acceptable.
The amount of these bills comes Rs.3,46,226/-.
The said amount is liable to be deducted from the total bills.
After deducted Rs.3,46,226/- from Rs.6,63,625/- it would be Rs.3,17,339/- which is rounded up at Rs.3,17,400/-.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,17,400/- as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
34. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement.

35. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr. Pratap Kumar Pani as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and he assessed disability.
Further, he got marked Case sheets at Ex.P.15 and 16.
He deposed that due to fusion of cervical spine there is a restricted movement of the neck and same has caused certain restriction to the whole body movement.
But he has not assessed disability.
36. In the cross-examination, PW.2 has admitted that he has not treated the patient at any point of time.
Further he admitted that after 13 years from the date of accident he has examined the petitioner.
He further says that with difficulty the petitioner is walking.
37. It is relevant to state here that the accident had occurred in the year 2009.
The petitioner has produced his IT returns forms for the year 2007-2008 to 2019-2020.
These documents show that his income has been gradually increased even after accident.
Even in the cross-examination, PW.1 admitted that he is running his business till date.
If this factor is taken into consideration, it is clear that the result of accident has no impact on the earning of the petitioner from his avocation.
This factor also justifies that as a result of accident PW.1 has not sustained any financial loss.

38. It is profitable to refer the judgment of Hon'ble High court of Karnataka reported in 2020 (4)
KCCR 221 between Sri.Nandish.K Vs United India Insurance Co. Ltd & another, wherein it is held that no compensation could be awarded towards the loss of earning capacity if physically disability do not effect claimant's capacity to work.

39. In the case of the Jithendran (supra) Hon'ble Supreme Court held are as follows:
"19.

Before parting, it needs emphasizing that in cases such as this, the Tribunal and the Courts must be conscious of the fact that the permanent disability suffered by the individual not only impairs his cognitive abilities and his physical facilities but there Raghavendra Ramarao Kulhalli vs Umesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152634601/
10 are multiple other non- quantifiable implications for the victim.

entities.text: Raghavendra Ramarao Kulhalli vs Umesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The very fact that a healthy person turns into an invalid, being deprived of normal companionship, and incapable of leading a productive life, makes one suffer the loss of self-dignity.
Such a Claimant must not be viewed as a modern day Oliver Twist, having to make entreaties as the boy in the orphanage in Charles Dickens's classic, "Please Sir, I want some more".
The efforts must be to substantially ameliorate the misery of the claimant and recognize his actual needs by accounting for the ground realities.
The measures should however be in correct proportion.

As is aptly said by Justice R.V Raveendran, while speaking for the Division Bench in Sarla Verma and Others Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and Another8, just compensation is adequate compensation and the Award must be just that- no less and no more.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma and Others Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and Another8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The plea 8 (2009)6 SCC 121 of the victim suffering from a cruel twist of fate, when asking for some more, is not extravagant but is for seeking appropriate recompense to negotiate with the unforeseeable and the fortuitous twists is his impaired life.

Therefore, while the money awarded by Courts can hardly redress the actual sufferings of the injured victim (who is deprived of the normal amenities of life and suffers the unease of being a burden on others), the courts can make a genuine attempt to help restore the self-dignity of such claimant, by awarding 'just compensation'."
40.
The above said authority deals about assessment of functional disability.
But in the case on hand physically disability of petitioner do not effect his capacity to work.
Hence the judgment relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner would not help the case of petitioner.
41. For the aforesaid reasons this Tribunal held that the petitioner is not entitled for any loss of future income under this head since he continues the job.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
42.

1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40,000/-

43. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-Z-9024 and negligent act of the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-01-C-4687.
44.
The Petition shows the Policy to both vehicles are valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
But insurer of the car bearing No.KA- 04Z-9024 contended that the petitioner was travelling in the private car for hire and rewarding violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
The petitioner has specifically denied such suggestions in his cross examination.
He specifically says that he was travelling with Shenoy who is the proprietor of the respondent No.2 company for business purpose i.e., company business.
Even officer of the respondent No.2 company in his cross examination dated 18.07.2024 admitted that travelers in the said car at the time of accident were related to his company.
Therefore, it is proved that the petitioner was travelling in the said car for the company business purpose.
Hence, there is no violation of policy.
Therefore, respondent No.2,3,5 and 6 being owners and insurer of both the vehicles are jointly are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Respondent No.1 and 4 are drivers of both the vehicles are not liable to pay compensation.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
45. ISSUE No.3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.2, 3, 5 and 6 U/Sec.
166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The claim petition filed against the Respondent No.1 and 4 is dismissed.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.4,60,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.2, 3, 5 and 6 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

The Respondent No.3 and 6 being the insurers of the offending vehicles, are directed to deposit 50%
each, the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.3 and 6, entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled principle of law that in a claim for compensation under sec. 166 of MV Act, the claimant has to prove the accident only on preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2011 SAR (Civil)
319 between Kusum & Ors vs Satbir & Ors.
12. Keeping the aforesaid principles in mind considered the evidence on record.
The respondents have not chosen to lead evidence of drivers of both the vehicles i.e., car and truck.
They are the best persons to speak about the manner of accident and negligence aspect is concerned.
But they have not stepped into witness box to prove their non negligence.
The allegation against the driver of the truck is without indicator or parking lights parked the lorry on the public road.
As such he has admitted his negligence.
The police documents available on record do not show that the lorry was parked by taking precaution.
The respondent No.4 driver of the truck and respondent No.5 the owner of the truck have not placed any materials to show that the lorry had been parked with tail lights or blinkers or self radiating triangles or guard or other devise to warn the vehicles.
By considering all these facts, it is crystal clear that lorry had been parked on the public road without taking any precaution and the driver of the car had dashed against the said lorry from back side.
Therefore, the driver of the truck had contributed for the accident.
The driver of the car had not challenged the charge sheet.
These aspects show that there is gross negligence on part the driver of the car and for the aforesaid reasons there is gross negligence on part of the driver of the lorry who parked on the road without precaution.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the driver (Respondent No.1) of the car attributed 50% of negligence towards the said accident.
Further, the driver (Respondent No.4) of the Truck attributed 50% of the negligence towards the said accident.
He has not produced any document to prove his age.
If this factor is taken into consideration, it is clear that the result of accident has no impact on the earning of the petitioner from his avocation.
This factor also justifies that as a result of accident PW.1 has not sustained any financial loss.
Before parting, it needs emphasizing that in cases such as this, the Tribunal and the Courts must be conscious of the fact that the permanent disability suffered by the individual not only impairs his cognitive abilities and his physical facilities but there Raghavendra Ramarao Kulhalli vs Umesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152634601/
10 are multiple other non- quantifiable implications for the victim.
The very fact that a healthy person turns into an invalid, being deprived of normal companionship, and incapable of leading a productive life, makes one suffer the loss of self-dignity.
The efforts must be to substantially ameliorate the misery of the claimant and recognize his actual needs by accounting for the ground realities.
As is aptly said by Justice R.V Raveendran, while speaking for the Division Bench in Sarla Verma and Others Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and Another8, just compensation is adequate compensation and the Award must be just that- no less and no more.
The plea 8 (2009)6 SCC 121 of the victim suffering from a cruel twist of fate, when asking for some more, is not extravagant but is for seeking appropriate recompense to negotiate with the unforeseeable and the fortuitous twists is his impaired life.
Therefore, while the money awarded by Courts can hardly redress the actual sufferings of the injured victim (who is deprived of the normal amenities of life and suffers the unease of being a burden on others), the courts can make a genuine attempt to help restore the self-dignity of such claimant, by awarding 'just compensation'."
